output.brief: Volunteers are leaving because of two changes combined, not either one alone. The app (basic tier) has no recurring bookings, so a regular keeps a weekly slot only if staff book it before the Thursday release. After the coordinator posts were cut on 1 May, that booking nearly stopped: about 74 a week at Dock Street and Westgate fell to 3, and one admin seat sits unused. Regulars then lost their usual slots to new sign-ups. 88% of those who lost slots twice or more are now inactive, against 11% who kept theirs. Millbrook has the app but kept its coordinator, and its numbers are stable. Quarry Lane lost its coordinator but has no app live, and is also stable. The background-check renewal doesn't explain it, because 121 of 123 lapsed volunteers had a current check. Commonplate shows little sign of being a cause. Don't cancel RotaWeave, which would cost $14k and leave the cause untouched. Don't suspend the checks, and don't purge inactive names from the roster. Instead, have someone book regulars into their usual slots at Dock Street and Westgate before each Thursday release, phone lapsed volunteers to offer their slot back, and review after 60 days. Confidence is high. The remaining gaps are Quarry Lane's go-live in October and the Commonplate posts, which I didn't read.
